paper.title: Algorithm 885: Computing the logarithm of the normal distribution
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 35(3), Article 20 (TOMS 885, Oct 2008)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 885.zip (fetched 2026-11-26, HTTP 200, 18179 bytes; sha256 4415d85ac688c4f1882f5b6100d9e8243d525c13cd65c9a8d93f40b44e544205)
code.note: C sources in 885/C (lnnorm.c is Algorithm 304 modified for log of the normal distribution; main.c is the driver; norminc.h holds constants). The driver checktable() reads the shipped table 885/C/sheppard.txt (Table IV of Sheppard 1939, 16 significant digits) and compares -lnnorm(-x) with it. The paper (ACM DL) has not been read by scout.

claim.location: The shipped reference table C/sheppard.txt in the 885.zip archive, row x = 5.0: '5.0    15.0649983939887257' (Sheppard 1939, Table IV, as cited by the article).
claim.metric: The value -lnnorm(-5.0) computed by C/lnnorm.c (the function the driver's checktable() tests as lnx = -lnnorm(-xf) with xf = 5.0), compared with the tabulated 15.0649983939887257.
claim.paper_value: Not used: the paper is paywalled and was not read. The claim rests on the shipped table only.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The table is printed to 16 significant digits, so its own rounding is about 1e-16 relative. 1.5e-8 absolute is 1e-9 relative at 15.065; a double-precision implementation of Algorithm 304 with the archive's constants should agree far better, and the margin covers libm and compiler differences. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: one C file compile and a single lnnorm call at x = -5.0.
cost.data_size: None; the reference table ships in the archive (sheppard.txt, a few KB).
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence of the archive; the rerun should record the licence text in the archive.

why: lnnorm computes a log tail probability by a rational approximation with no closed form at x = -5, and the archive's own table of 1939 values is a checkable reference for the same function the driver tests.
